found_in_own_draft.what: The listing copy described Assumptions as 'every rate and constant in one editable place'. The sheet is a list of excluded and included statements with a location and an owner note; the editable rates and constants live in Setup.
found_in_own_draft.found_by: comparing the copy line by line with the sheet headers
found_in_own_draft.fix: Copy now describes what the sheet actually contains and where the numbers live.

found_in_own_draft.what: The listing copy asserted the workbook works in 'Excel, LibreOffice Calc or Google Sheets'. Only Excel and openpyxl were ever exercised; the other two are untested, so the claim was stronger than the evidence.
found_in_own_draft.found_by: checking the copy against the build report's own UNKNOWN list
found_in_own_draft.fix: Copy now says it is built for Excel, states that the other two are untested, and invites the buyer to report any problem.

found_in_own_draft.what: Summary!B19 was labelled 'All-in plan (revised budget + reserve)' but its formula added B14, the reserve that is left, so it displayed $49,700 rather than the $51,800 the label implied. The guide repeated the same claim ('adds the reserve back'), and the $2,100 already drawn from the reserve appeared nowhere on the one-page Summary, so money already spent was invisible there.
found_in_own_draft.found_by: auditing the label against its own formula and against the guide sentence repeating it
found_in_own_draft.fix: Label is now '(revised budget + reserve left)'; new Summary!B20 'Contingency drawn to date' =Contingency!$H$2; guide paragraph 11 and the worked-example paragraph corrected; listing copy names the new row; the Excel probe and the independent model now compare 17 fields instead of 16.

process_incident.fix: GF_PDF_IMPORT_ONLY guard in build_batch12_pdfs.py; the B13 guide loader sets it before importing.
